MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sample Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Clinical Indication: Diagnostic testing for Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT)

CLINICAL DETAILS
Adult patient referred for genetic testing to investigate suspected Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia.

TEST METHODOLOGY
1. Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA)
   - Analysis for whole exon deletions/duplications in BMPR2, ALK-1/ACVRL1, and ENG genes
   - MLPA kit: GeneScan-P09 for targeted exon analysis
   - All exons of the three genes analyzed for copy number variations

2. Bi-directional Sanger Sequencing
   - Complete sequencing of all coding regions and intron-exon boundaries
   - Genes analyzed: ALK-1/ACVRL1 (NM_000020.3) and ENG (NM_001114753.2)
   - Point mutation screening including splice site analysis

RESULTS

Gene: BMPR2 (NM_001204.7)
MLPA Analysis: No exon deletions or duplications detected
Sequencing: Not performed

Gene: ALK-1/ACVRL1 (NM_000020.3)
MLPA Analysis: No exon deletions or duplications detected
Sequencing: No pathogenic variants identified in coding regions or splice sites
Coverage: 100% of coding sequence at >30x depth

Gene: ENG (NM_001114753.2)
MLPA Analysis: No exon deletions or duplications detected
Sequencing: No pathogenic variants identified in coding regions or splice sites
Coverage: 100% of coding sequence at >30x depth

INTERPRETATION
No mutations were detected in the BMPR2, ALK-1/ACVRL1, or ENG genes by either MLPA analysis or bi-directional sequencing. The complete examination of coding regions and splice sites of ALK-1 and ENG revealed no pathogenic variants. MLPA analysis showed no abnormalities in exon-level copy number for any of the three genes tested.

The clinical diagnosis of Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia has not been confirmed genetically by this analysis. However, this negative result does not exclude the diagnosis of HHT.

TEST LIMITATIONS
- This analysis is limited to the coding regions and immediate splice sites of ALK-1/ACVRL1 and ENG genes
- Deep intronic variants and regulatory region mutations are not detected by this methodology
- BMPR2 was analyzed by MLPA only; point mutations in BMPR2 would not be detected
- Mutations in other genes associated with HHT (e.g., SMAD4, GDF2) were not analyzed
- The analytical sensitivity for detecting heterozygous sequence variants is >99%

RECOMMENDATIONS
These results do not exclude a diagnosis of HHT, as mutations in genes not included in this analysis may be responsible for the clinical phenotype. If clinical suspicion remains high, the following options should be considered:
1. Extended genetic panel testing including SMAD4 and GDF2 genes
2. Clinical diagnosis based on Curaçao criteria
3. Genetic counseling to discuss implications for family members
4. Consider research-based whole exome or genome sequencing if diagnosis remains uncertain

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
